mappings.note: Both serve as the title/introduction identifying David and the location (Juda's wilderness).
Translation includes 'au point du jour' (at daybreak) which is not present in the OSMAIN text. The rest matches the thirst and longing description.
Both describe seeking God in the sanctuary to see power and glory.
Both state grace is better than life and lips will praise.
Both describe blessing God while living and lifting hands in His name.
Both describe the soul being satisfied like marrow/fat and joyful praise.
Both describe remembering God on the bed and meditating during night watches.
Both state God was a help and the soul rejoices under His wings' shadow.
Translation adds 'pour te suivre' (to follow you) which is not in the OSMAIN text. The core meaning of clinging and being upheld by the right hand matches.
Both describe enemies seeking to destroy life descending into the earth's depths.

The OSMAIN verse 11 contains three distinct thoughts: falling by the sword, becoming prey for foxes, AND the king rejoicing/lies being silenced. The translation splits this into two verses (v11 and v12).
This verse contains the second half of OSMAIN verse 11 (King rejoicing, oath-takers glorifying, liars silenced).

extraContent.description: Phrase 'au point du jour' (at daybreak) is present in translation but absent in OSMAIN v2.
Phrase 'pour te suivre' (to follow you) is present in translation but absent in OSMAIN v9.
